_help: How CVs and cover letters are usually written, by market (country group), sector and level. engine/conventions.py picks the market from the posting's location, the sector from its category and title, and the level from its seniority, then merges market + sector + level (later ones add to or replace earlier ones). Override or extend any part in your own inputs/document_conventions.json. These are common practice, not law, except where a rule says so; when a posting asks for something specific, the posting wins. A market's must_not_contain list is checked like tailoring_checks (a document containing one of them is not rendered).

nordic.label: Nordic (Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Iceland)
nordic.spelling: British English (or the local language if the posting is in it)
nordic.photo: usually omitted (more common in Denmark); never needed
nordic.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city; no date of birth, marital status, ID number or photo unless asked
nordic.work_authorization: state it briefly if you are not an EU/EEA citizen (for example permanent residence)
nordic.tone: factual, modest and concrete; no superlatives or self-promotion; show collaboration and how you work
nordic.metrics: sparingly: only verified results that the posting values; research postings welcome one or two per project
nordic.profile_section: a short profile of 3-4 lines is usual
nordic.references: 'References available upon request' is acceptable; names only when asked

letter.salutation: Dear Hiring Manager, (or the contact person's name)
letter.focus: why this employer and team, what you would contribute, how you work with others; avoid repeating the CV

nordic.language: write in the posting's language; Swedish/Norwegian/Danish postings usually expect the local language unless they say English is fine
notes: Employers value balance, teamwork and practical results more than personal branding.

dach.label: Germany, Austria, Switzerland
dach.spelling: British or US English used consistently; German if the posting is in German
dach.date_format: MM/YYYY in the CV, DD.MM.YYYY in the letter
dach.photo: traditionally common in Germany and Austria, but optional and not legally required; omit for international companies
dach.personal_details: name, address, phone, e-mail; date of birth and nationality are traditional but optional
dach.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA (or Swiss) citizen
dach.tone: formal, precise, complete; exact dates; no unexplained gaps
dach.references: not listed; work certificates (Arbeitszeugnisse) and degree certificates are often attached

letter.focus: formal motivation letter (Anschreiben): position, qualifications that match, earliest start date and salary expectation if the posting asks

dach.language: German postings expect German documents unless English is stated
notes: A traditional German CV (Lebenslauf) is tabular, reverse-chronological, and ends with place, date and signature; international employers do not expect the signature.

uk_ie.label: United Kingdom and Ireland
uk_ie.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, town; omit date of birth, age, marital status, photo (UK equality law makes employers avoid these)
uk_ie.work_authorization: state right to work or visa status if relevant
uk_ie.profile_section: a personal profile/statement of 3-5 lines at the top is usual
uk_ie.references: 'References available on request', or two referees when asked

letter.closing: Yours sincerely, (with a name) / Kind regards,
letter.focus: match the essential criteria of the job description point by point

notes: Public sector and university posts often require a supporting statement that addresses each criterion of the person specification.

us.label: United States
us.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city and state, LinkedIn/portfolio; never date of birth, age, photo, marital status, nationality or religion (US equal-employment rules make employers avoid them)
us.work_authorization: state visa or sponsorship needs only when relevant, briefly (for example 'Requires H-1B sponsorship')
us.tone: confident and achievement-oriented; every bullet starts with an action verb
us.metrics: expected: quantify impact (%, time, cost, scale, performance) wherever the material verifies it
us.profile_section: a 2-3 line summary is optional; skills section with the posting's exact keywords (applicant tracking systems)
us.references: omit; never write 'References available upon request'

letter.focus: the value you bring to the team's problems; direct and specific

notes: Industry uses a 'resume'; 'CV' means the long academic document. Use the posting's terminology for titles and skills so applicant tracking systems match them.

canada.label: Canada
canada.spelling: Canadian English (British-style spellings such as 'colour', '-ize' accepted)
canada.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city and province; no date of birth, age, photo, marital status (human-rights codes)
canada.work_authorization: state citizenship, permanent residence or work permit status briefly if relevant
canada.tone: professional and achievement-oriented, somewhat less assertive than the US
canada.profile_section: short summary of qualifications is usual

letter.focus: fit with the role and the organization

canada.language: English; in Quebec, French is expected unless the posting is in English

australia_nz.label: Australia and New Zealand
australia_nz.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, suburb/city; no date of birth, age, photo, marital status
australia_nz.work_authorization: state citizenship, permanent residency or visa (with work rights) clearly; it is often asked
australia_nz.profile_section: a career summary/objective of 3-4 lines is usual
australia_nz.references: two referees, often with contact details, or 'available on request'

letter.focus: the role's key requirements; public sector and universities ask for a separate statement addressing each selection criterion

notes: Selection criteria statements (often 1-2 pages, one heading per criterion, with concrete examples) are common for government and university jobs.

france.label: France and French-speaking postings
france.spelling: French if the posting is in French; British or US English otherwise
france.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city; age and photo optional
france.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA citizen
france.profile_section: a one-line title and a short profile are usual

letter.closing: formal closing formula in French letters (Je vous prie d'agréer...); 'Kind regards,' in English
letter.focus: lettre de motivation: you, them, us; formal register

france.language: French postings expect French documents unless English is stated

benelux.label: Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg
benelux.spelling: British or US English used consistently; Dutch/French/German if the posting is in it
benelux.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city; date of birth optional
benelux.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA citizen
benelux.tone: direct, concise and to the point (especially in the Netherlands)

letter.focus: short and specific: why this job, what you bring

benelux.language: Dutch postings in the Netherlands often accept English for technical roles; Belgian postings follow the region's language

southern_europe.label: Spain, Italy, Portugal, Greece, Malta, Cyprus
southern_europe.spelling: British English (or the local language if the posting is in it)
southern_europe.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city; date of birth and nationality traditional but optional
southern_europe.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA citizen

data_consent_clause.IT: Autorizzo il trattamento dei dati personali contenuti nel mio curriculum vitae in base al Regolamento UE 2016/679 (GDPR).

notes: In Italy a data-processing consent sentence at the end of the CV is customary; Europass format is common in the public sector.

central_eastern.label: Central and Eastern Europe and the Baltics
central_eastern.spelling: British or US English used consistently; the local language if the posting is in it
central_eastern.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA citizen
central_eastern.language: the posting's language; English is common for international companies

data_consent_clause.PL: I agree to the processing of personal data provided in this document for realising the recruitment process pursuant to the Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR).

notes: In Poland a GDPR consent sentence at the end of the CV is customary and often requested in the posting.

international.label: Other or unknown country (neutral international style)
international.spelling: British or US English used consistently

industry.label: Industry
industry.publications: a short 'Selected publications' (2-4) only if the role is research-oriented; otherwise leave out
industry.emphasis: products, systems and results you delivered; tools and methods the posting names; scope and responsibility

academia.label: Academia (PhD, postdoc, researcher, lecturer, professor)
academia.publications: complete list with exact titles, venues and years from the authoritative source, grouped by type (journal, conference, other); mark your own name
academia.references: usually two or three referees with title, affiliation and e-mail

letter.focus: fit with the group's research, your main results, what you plan to do there, and teaching where relevant

extras: research statement or plan when asked
teaching statement when asked (US faculty posts)
publication list as a separate file when asked
academia.emphasis: research contributions, publications, independence, supervision and teaching, funding
academia.metrics: research results (performance, efficiency, citations of the work) are welcome; give one or two per project

junior.label: Junior / graduate / entry
junior.emphasis: education, thesis and projects first or near the top; internships and part-time roles count; skills with where they were used

mid.label: Experienced / mid-level
mid.emphasis: most recent and most relevant roles in detail; education after experience
mid.older_roles: shorten roles older than about ten years

senior.label: Senior / staff / lead / principal / architect / manager
senior.emphasis: scope and ownership: systems or products you were responsible for, technical decisions, leading or mentoring, cross-team work, outcomes; a strong 3-4 line profile
senior.older_roles: one line each for early roles; drop very old ones
